packet.title: Parsing XPath: each text once, and a cheaper parse (implementation)

body.p: After (tree-sitter), (perf-3 for XML), and . XPath parsing is 30 % of compiling the EN 16931 Schematron (tree-sitter's ts_parser_parse 23 %). The official compiled stylesheet repeats its expressions: 3,228 test, select and match attributes, 1,049 distinct; the expanded Schematron less so (1,086 test and context attributes, 1,007 distinct).

item.p: Mechanism: profile first; parse each distinct expression text once per compilation where the static context is the same (an AST cache keyed by the text and the static context's identity; the lowering then takes a copy or shares an immutable AST, whichever the front end allows, and memory limits kept); then make the parse itself cheaper the way perf-3 did for XML (fewer tokens and nodes in the grammar, a cheaper walk), with the grammar's tests and every outcome unchanged.

Owns: src/xpath_parse.c, the XPath front end's AST building and its internal headers, grammars/xpath* (if the XPath grammar lives there), the XPath parser's tests, tests/bench/. Not the IR files (perf-16).

Done when: before and after (instructions and seconds) in a D-record on both invoice runs, xmark-all and the XT40 compile; the ASTs and the IR text identical; QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 whole, base and change in the same setup: no outcome changes, case by case; Schematron 463 of 463, VEFA 1,133. Done 2026-10-28 (): grammars/xpath inlines its hidden choice rules (operator levels, steps, primaries, names): 676 to 132 reductions for a typical assertion, same nodes; an AST memo per XSLT read and Schematron compile; fields kept per identifier. Invoice transform 1.618 to 1.291 x 10^9, validate 1.613 to 1.321; xmark-all 8.641 to 8.638; ASTs and IR text identical; XP40, XQ40, XT40 0 outcomes differ; suite 463/463, VEFA 1,133/1,133.
